what_taken: CSIRO study of Australian red meat greenhouse gas emissions: 124.1 Mt CO2e in 2005, 68.6 Mt in 2015, mostly from less land clearing (pp. 13, 15). Six pathways to 2030 hold cattle near 25 million, sheep 70 million, goats 0.5 million; feedlot cattle 2.8 million in 2015, 12% of herd (p. 14). Productivity trends for 1990 to 2010 are quoted from Wiedemann 2015a (p. 14). An emissions and cost study.

Productivity enters only through the Feedlot Futures pathway (earlier slaughter, heavier weights) and the cost model's productivity gains, which are in the SI appendix, not in the PDF (p. 15). what_taken: Gate-to-gate life cycle assessment of seven feedlots in Qld, NSW and Vic., records for 2007 and 2008, per kg liveweight gain (p. 1150). Short-fed, mid-fed, long-fed cattle: GHG 4.6, 5.2, 9.5 kg CO2-e; fossil energy 16.5, 18.9, 34.2 MJ; arable land 18.7, 22.5, 40.5 m2; fresh water 672.6, 554.6, 171.9 L (Table 9, p. 1155). Feed conversion ratio explains 0.95 of GHG variation (p. 1156). Long-fed class is one feedlot.

what_taken: Review of the northern Australian beef production cycle: maternal nutrition, weaning, backgrounding, feedlots, rumen microbes, carcass quality, aimed at listing research gaps (Introduction; Conclusion). Phosphorus deficiency is one theme among several (Highlights; Conclusion). National herd 23 million head (MLA 2020); northern share 49% (Highlights) or about 60% (Introduction). No herd productivity rates. PMC text without page numbers.

Household totals run 1.46 to 4.99 Mt; the bin-audit scale-up is under 30% of the ABS-based total (pp. 162-163). No mention of the National Food Waste Strategy.

what_taken: Online survey of 4,324 Australian households (June 2019, Fight Food Waste CRC, Dynata panel) asking what the household threw away in the past 7 days, in cups or slices across 11 food types (p. 4). Path model: planning -0.052, storing -0.108, disposal routines +0.179 on amount wasted; R-squared 0.065 for food waste (pp. 6-7). Amounts are self-reported counts, not kilograms; no national tonnage is given.

what_taken: Book chapter arguing that national grain reserves and open trade work together in food crises, drawing on rice in 2007-08 and grain in 2022 (pp. 229-230). Four price models, ending in a political economy model where domestic stocks build confidence in trade (pp. 231-232). Rough sum: one more week of rice stored by a billion households is 7 Mt, a quarter of annual rice trade (p. 234). No Australian figures.

what_taken: World Bank funded study of grain reserves for the Middle East and North Africa, prompted by the 2007-08 price spike (p. 61). Argues stocks beat self-sufficiency or foreign land in dry countries; size depends on supply diversity, supplier reliability, cost (pp. 71-72). Region imports a net 58.1 Mt of cereal; import share 56% in 2000, 63% projected for 2030 (p. 61). Saudi example: one or two years' supply (p. 72).

Identity confirmed: Wright and Cafiero, Food Security 3(Suppl 1):S61-S76, received 3 September 2010, published online 10 February 2011, open access. Page numbers are the printed S-numbers. The paper mentions the Australian drought as one of the shocks of 2007-08 (pp. 61, 63, 74) but treats no Australian reserve policy. Its virtual reserve figure of US$12 to 20 billion (p. 70) is a proposal by others that the paper discusses and is not taken.
